Japanese artist Taiki Yokote  , creates unsettling kinetic sculptures that blur the boundary between life and d**th. In Until You Become Soil, animal fur is assembled into a towering, irregular structure that continuously trembles and shifts, as though something beneath its surface were still alive. The movement comes from concealed massage devices that animate the fur of deceased animals, giving an eerie sense of renewed existence. The work originated from Yokote’s inability to discard the hair left behind by his beloved dog . #art #artist #fur #sculptureart #artistsoftiktok

Rachel Youn creates kinetic sculptures using artificial plants, electric massagers, metal structures, and everyday mechanical parts. Her works often make fake flowers shake, vibrate, and move like living organisms. The movement is simple, but it changes how we see the object. A decorative plant becomes a machine, a body, and a performance at the same time. Her sculptures question the line between nature, technology, decoration, and artificial life.#flower #plant #nature #art #artist

Danish artist Simon Lindbeej explores interaction and emergence through a kinetic cabinet that brings together magnetism, mirrors and shadow patterns. Developed since 2025, the work turns furniture into a dynamic system where components influence each other, generating shifting visual rhythms and unexpected formations. Meet Archetype This robotic arm blends human creativity with machine intelligence as it draws, writes, and mimics nature… then erases everything to begin again. The idea comes from the artist Roy Nachum’s childhood, when he sculpted in beach sand only to have each creation washed away by the waves — a reminder that every ending is also a new beginning. Guests are invited to channel that same inspiration and create their own art in the kinetic sand on both sides of the room.
